A1.justification: Both 34-page PDFs describe the same COD-TDQ work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantization experiments on CFRN and ESCNet across four COD datasets, including component ablations, sensitivity results and mechanism diagnostics.

after.justification: v2 retains original COD quantization results and reports additional CFRN runtime, latency and memory measurements in Table 5.

M1.justification: Appendix S3.1 adds a label-free procedure selecting group size and constraint bounds through calibration-forward feature drift and quantization diagnostics. v1 instead describes frozen settings and a sensitivity sweep. The core DSTG/DCRP quantizer, equations and Algorithm S1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate camouflaged-object detection on CAMO, CHAMELEON, COD10K and NC4K using CFRN and ESCNet. The new runtime evaluation introduces no additional dataset, population or task scenario.

E2.justification: Accuracy-comparison membership remains unchanged in Tables 2–3 and the full ESCNet table. Runtime comparison changes: v1 compares online COD-TDQ with a fixed offline-calibrated control, whereas v2 Table 5 compares against FP32, naive W4A4, PTQ4SAM, RepQ-ViT and IGQ-ViT.

E3.justification: Section 5.5 adds an end-to-end efficiency protocol described as a Triton INT4 path on RTX 4090, with 384×384 inputs, batch size 4, per-image latency and peak allocated GPU memory. v1 reports simulated throughput on RTX 2080Ti. These constitute substantially different runtime settings; the retained accuracy splits, metrics and shared hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 removes the hyperparameter sweep in v1 Figure S1, the fixed-calibration and C1-only/C2-only tests in Table S2, and the cross-dataset component ablations in Tables S4–S5. It revises the retained NC4K ablations and adds a DSTG runtime-overhead check. This substantially changes the evidence testing parameter sensitivity and component necessity.

E5.justification: Both retain the same disclosed default seeds, CFRN 0 and ESCNet 42, and state that calibration-size and random-seed sweeps are outside scope. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars.

E6.justification: Table 4 revises intermediate ablation scores: CFRN DSTG-only Sα changes from 0.458 to 0.451 and MAE from 0.112 to 0.270. Supplementary sensitivity and ablation results disappear, while Table 5 adds efficiency results, including COD-TDQ at 44.21 FPS and 22.61 ms/image. Main benchmark accuracy values remain unchanged. The CFRN DCRP row's changed name is not reconciled with its retained attention-only description.

T1.justification: The quantization definitions, dual constraints, boundary-heavy set construction, and Appendix S2.3 lemma, proposition and proofs are retained. Notational and punctuation edits do not change mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly qualifies the claimed 0.12–0.14 Sα improvement as CFRN-specific. The central failure diagnosis, DSTG/DCRP contributions and transferability claim remain unchanged; the abstract still retains its broader greater-than-0.12 wording.

C2.justification: Section 5.5 adds an interpretation of efficiency measurements as deployment benefits with only 0.6% DSTG overhead, whereas v1 confines runtime conclusions to simulated execution. Parameter-specific sensitivity explanations are removed. The new deployment framing conflicts with retained appendix statements that native INT4 execution is outside the evidence.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a code-release promise with a concrete repository address. Section 5.5 adds deployment configuration, 69.73% Triton operator coverage, and packing and metadata-overhead details. The explicit statement that calibration image IDs are listed in released code disappears, while most implementation documentation remains unchanged.

R1.justification: The reference list expands from 50 to 61 entries, adding works including CATP, SelectQ and branch convolution quantization. These additions broaden citations within existing introductory and related-work passages without substantially changing the positioning around token-local activation failures.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammatical corrections, adds Section 5.5, rewrites Appendix S3.1, removes the empty Algorithm subsection and separate Frozen Setting subsection, and shortens the conclusion and acknowledgements. Most exposition and section ordering remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds runtime Table 5, removes v1 Figure S1 and Tables S2, S4 and S5, and adjusts float placement. Figure 3 replaces the CoDA-Q labels with COD-TDQ. Surviving appendix histograms and qualitative displays are retained under new numbering, with the overall visual design unchanged.

improvement.justification: The code address and new efficiency measurements offer useful additions, but v2 removes sensitivity and constraint-specific ablation evidence supporting parameter choices and the dual-constraint rationale. Section 5.5's real-INT4 framing conflicts with Appendix S1.2 and Table S9, and revised ablation labels remain inconsistent with control definitions. These substantive tradeoffs and unresolved reporting conflicts prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
